claude.sample_unit: simulated episodes per condition (5 synthetic cases x 20 repeats)

links.outcome: Case fidelity and hit rate under direct injection with vs without string-level sanitizer
links.effect: Direct contamination fidelity 0.098 and hit rate 0.077; with sanitizer 0.945 and 0.942. Indirect contamination had near-clean fidelity (0.946) so defense added minimal benefit; leakage persisted ~0.60/episode.
links.quote: The defense preprocessing step restored direct-contamination performance to near-clean levels (slot-level F1 score, 0.945; 95% CI, 0.938-0.952; hit rate, 0.942; 95% CI, 0.930-0.955).

links.outcome: Robustness to adversarial contaminated inputs with input sanitization defense
links.effect: Direct contamination collapsed fidelity to 0.098 (hit rate 0.077); input sanitizer restored fidelity to 0.945 and hit rate to 0.942 without refusals.
links.quote: Under direct contamination, case fidelity improved from 0.098 to 0.945, and turn-target hit rate improved from 0.077 to 0.942 after defense.

links.outcome: Performance under noisy (typo-corrupted) inputs and contamination vs clean inputs
links.effect: Noise preserved fidelity (0.941 vs 0.947) but reduced turn-target hit rate to 0.823 from 0.946; direct contamination dropped fidelity to 0.098.
links.quote: Noise preserved case fidelity (0.941; 95% CI, 0.934-0.949) but reduced turn-target hit rate (0.823; 95% CI, 0.806-0.841).

links.outcome: Forbidden information leakage and role drift of virtual patient LLM within intended role boundaries
links.effect: Forbidden leakage ~0.60 events per episode in clean condition (95% CI 0.502-0.698); role drift not observed; refusal/clarification 0.
links.quote: However, forbidden information leakage occurred at approximately 0.60 events per episode under the clean condition (0.600; 95% CI, 0.502-0.698), indicating incomplete constraint adherence despite high case fidelity.
